cues.en: In this chapter, we want to have a look at how for loops work in Bash.
For loops, allow us to repeat a block of code and it sounds like we pretty much have had a look at
that already through our While loops.
But the while loops they had a few problems with a while loop.
What we had looked at already.
We had to make sure that we don't end up in an endless loop.
So it was up to US programmers to ensure that the while loop eventually terminates, to add a break
at some point, or to check the condition properly that we don't end up in an endless loop.
Also, if we had, let's say, several elements that we want to have a look at, we had to manage those
elements or those variables manually and we had to keep track of what the loop should do.
For loops, solve this for us.
If we know ahead of time how often we want the loop to be executed and they are optimized for this and
they also keep track of the elements for us.
So they are optimized for this use case.
In this chapter we will have a look at for loops and we will also have a look at common use cases for
